problems.title: Verify if P or NP

description.en:
Given a list of computational problems, classify each as belonging to class P or class NP (but not known to be in P). For each problem, print 'P' if it can be solved in polynomial time, or 'NP' if it can only be verified in polynomial time but no known polynomial-time solution exists.

Problems to classify:
1. Sorting an array
2. Subset Sum
3. Binary Search
4. Hamiltonian Cycle
5. Shortest Path (Dijkstra)
6. Graph Coloring (k >= 3)
7. Matrix Multiplication
8. Travelling Salesman (Decision)
description.hi:
Computational problems ki ek list di gayi hai, har ek ko class P ya class NP (jo P mein nahi hai abhi tak) mein classify karo. Har problem ke liye 'P' print karo agar ye polynomial time mein solve ho sakti hai, ya 'NP' print karo agar ye sirf polynomial time mein verify ho sakti hai lekin koi known polynomial-time solution nahi hai.

Classify karne ke liye problems:
1. Array sorting
2. Subset Sum
3. Binary Search
4. Hamiltonian Cycle
5. Shortest Path (Dijkstra)
6. Graph Coloring (k >= 3)
7. Matrix Multiplication
8. Travelling Salesman (Decision)

explanation.en: Sorting can be done in O(n log n) which is polynomial time
explanation.hi: Sorting O(n log n) mein ho sakti hai jo polynomial time hai

explanation.en: No known polynomial time algorithm exists, but a solution can be verified in O(n)
explanation.hi: Koi known polynomial time algorithm nahi hai, lekin solution O(n) mein verify ho sakta hai

constraints: Each problem name is a valid computational problem

hints.en: P problems have known polynomial algorithms. Think about which common algorithms you know.
hints.hi: P problems ke known polynomial algorithms hain. Socho kaunse common algorithms tumhe pata hain.

hints.en: NP-Complete problems like SAT, Subset Sum, TSP, Hamiltonian Cycle are all in NP but not known to be in P
hints.hi: NP-Complete problems jaise SAT, Subset Sum, TSP, Hamiltonian Cycle sab NP mein hain lekin P mein hain ya nahi pata nahi

n = int(input())

approach.en: Use a lookup of known P and NP problems. Sorting, searching, shortest path, matrix multiplication are in P. Subset Sum, Hamiltonian Cycle, Graph Coloring, TSP are NP-Complete (in NP, not known to be in P).
approach.hi: Known P aur NP problems ka lookup use karo. Sorting, searching, shortest path, matrix multiplication P mein hain. Subset Sum, Hamiltonian Cycle, Graph Coloring, TSP NP-Complete hain (NP mein hain, P mein hain ya nahi pata nahi).

description.en: Given a set of n non-negative integers and a target sum, determine if there exists a subset of the given set whose sum is exactly equal to the target. Print 'YES' if such a subset exists, otherwise print 'NO'. This is a classic NP-Complete problem.
description.hi: n non-negative integers ka ek set diya hai aur ek target sum hai. Batao ki kya given set ka koi aisa subset hai jiska sum exactly target ke barabar hai. Agar aisa subset hai toh 'YES' print karo, warna 'NO'. Ye ek classic NP-Complete problem hai.

explanation.en: No subset sums to 11. Maximum possible sum is 6.
explanation.hi: Koi subset 11 nahi banata. Maximum possible sum 6 hai.

hints.en: For small n, try all 2^n subsets using bitmask or recursion
hints.hi: Chhote n ke liye 2^n saare subsets try karo bitmask ya recursion se

hints.en: Dynamic programming approach: dp[i][j] = can we make sum j using first i elements?
hints.hi: Dynamic programming approach: dp[i][j] = kya hum pehle i elements se sum j bana sakte hain?

problems.title: Vertex Cover

description.en:
Given an undirected graph with n vertices and m edges, find the minimum vertex cover - the smallest set of vertices such that every edge in the graph has at least one endpoint in the set. Since finding the exact minimum vertex cover is NP-Complete, implement a 2-approximation algorithm.

Print the size of the vertex cover found, followed by the vertices in the cover (sorted).
description.hi:
Ek undirected graph diya hai jisme n vertices aur m edges hain. Minimum vertex cover dhundho - vertices ka sabse chhota set jisme graph ki har edge ka kam se kam ek endpoint ho. Kyunki exact minimum vertex cover dhundhna NP-Complete hai, ek 2-approximation algorithm implement karo.

Vertex cover ka size print karo, phir cover mein vertices (sorted) print karo.

explanation.en: The 2-approximation picks edges and adds both endpoints. Actual minimum cover could be {0, 3} (size 2), but approximation guarantees at most 2x optimal.
explanation.hi: 2-approximation edges pick karke dono endpoints add karta hai. Actual minimum cover {0, 3} (size 2) ho sakta hai, lekin approximation guarantee karta hai ki optimal se 2x se zyada nahi hoga.

constraints: Graph has no self-loops or duplicate edges

hints.en: Pick any uncovered edge, add BOTH endpoints to cover, remove all edges incident to these vertices
hints.hi: Koi uncovered edge pick karo, DONO endpoints ko cover mein daalo, in vertices se connected saari edges hatao

hints.en: This greedy approach gives at most 2x the optimal vertex cover size
hints.hi: Ye greedy approach optimal vertex cover size ka zyaada se zyaada 2 guna deta hai

starterCode.python:
def vertex_cover(n, edges):
    # Implement 2-approximation vertex cover
    # Write your code here
    pass

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = []
for _ in range(m):
    u, v = map(int, input().split())
    edges.append((u, v))
cover = vertex_cover(n, edges)
print(len(cover))
print(*sorted(cover))

approach.en: 2-Approximation: While there are uncovered edges, pick an arbitrary edge (u,v), add both u and v to the cover, and remove all edges incident to u or v. The result is at most 2x optimal.
approach.hi: 2-Approximation: Jab tak uncovered edges hain, ek arbitrary edge (u,v) pick karo, u aur v dono ko cover mein daalo, aur u ya v se connected saari edges hatao. Result optimal se zyaada se zyaada 2 guna hoga.

solution.timeComplexity: O(m^2) for naive, O(m) with adjacency list

description.en:
Given an undirected graph with n vertices and m edges, determine if the graph can be properly colored using at most k colors such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color. Print 'YES' if possible, 'NO' otherwise.

A proper coloring assigns a color to each vertex so that for every edge (u, v), vertex u and vertex v have different colors. This is the k-colorability decision problem, which is NP-Complete for k >= 3.
description.hi:
Ek undirected graph diya hai jisme n vertices aur m edges hain. Batao ki kya graph ko zyaada se zyaada k colors se properly color kiya ja sakta hai taaki koi do adjacent vertices ka same color na ho. Agar possible hai toh 'YES' print karo, warna 'NO'.

Proper coloring mein har vertex ko ek color assign hota hai taaki har edge (u, v) ke liye, u aur v ka color alag ho. Ye k-colorability decision problem hai, jo k >= 3 ke liye NP-Complete hai.

explanation.en: Color 0->Red, 1->Blue, 2->Red, 3->Blue. A cycle of even length needs only 2 colors.
explanation.hi: Color 0->Red, 1->Blue, 2->Red, 3->Blue. Even length cycle ko sirf 2 colors chahiye.

explanation.en: This is K4 (complete graph on 4 vertices), needs 4 colors. Cannot be done with 2.
explanation.hi: Ye K4 hai (4 vertices ka complete graph), 4 colors chahiye. 2 se nahi ho sakta.

hints.en: Use backtracking: try assigning each color (1 to k) to each vertex and check if the assignment is valid
hints.hi: Backtracking use karo: har vertex ko har color (1 se k) assign karke dekho ki assignment valid hai ya nahi

hints.en: Pruning: if a vertex's neighbor already has a color, don't try that color for the current vertex
hints.hi: Pruning: agar vertex ke neighbor ka color already assign hai, toh current vertex ke liye wo color mat try karo

starterCode.python:
def can_color(adj, n, k):
    # Determine if graph can be colored with k colors
    # Write your code here
    pass

n, m, k = map(int, input().split())
adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
for _ in range(m):
    u, v = map(int, input().split())
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
print("YES" if can_color(adj, n, k) else "NO")

approach.en: Use backtracking. Try to assign colors 1..k to vertices one by one. For each vertex, try each color and check if any neighbor has the same color. If valid, recurse to the next vertex. If no color works, backtrack.
approach.hi: Backtracking use karo. Vertices ko ek ek karke colors 1..k assign karne ki koshish karo. Har vertex ke liye, har color try karo aur check karo ki kisi neighbor ka same color toh nahi. Agar valid hai toh next vertex pe recurse karo. Agar koi color kaam nahi karta, toh backtrack karo.

solution.timeComplexity: O(k^n) worst case (exponential, as expected for NP-Complete)

description.en:
Given a complete graph with n cities and the distance between every pair of cities, find an approximate solution to the Travelling Salesman Problem using the Nearest Neighbor heuristic.

The salesman must visit every city exactly once and return to the starting city (city 0), minimizing the total travel distance.

Since TSP is NP-Complete, implement the Nearest Neighbor heuristic: from the current city, always go to the nearest unvisited city.

Print the total distance of the tour found, followed by the order of cities visited.
description.hi:
Ek complete graph diya hai jisme n cities hain aur har pair of cities ke beech distance diya hai. Travelling Salesman Problem ka approximate solution Nearest Neighbor heuristic se dhundho.

Salesman ko har city exactly ek baar visit karna hai aur starting city (city 0) pe wapas aana hai, total travel distance minimize karke.

Kyunki TSP NP-Complete hai, Nearest Neighbor heuristic implement karo: current city se hamesha sabse nearest unvisited city pe jao.

Tour ka total distance print karo, phir cities ka visit order print karo.

explanation.en: Starting at 0: nearest is 1 (dist=10), from 1 nearest unvisited is 3 (dist=25), from 3 nearest unvisited is 2 (dist=30), return to 0 (dist=15). Total = 10+25+30+15 = 80.
explanation.hi: 0 se start: nearest 1 hai (dist=10), 1 se nearest unvisited 3 hai (dist=25), 3 se nearest unvisited 2 hai (dist=30), 0 pe wapas (dist=15). Total = 10+25+30+15 = 80.

hints.en: Start at city 0, mark it visited. At each step, find the nearest unvisited city and move there.
hints.hi: City 0 se start karo, visited mark karo. Har step pe nearest unvisited city dhundho aur wahan jao.

hints.en: Don't forget to add the distance from the last city back to city 0
hints.hi: Last city se city 0 ka distance add karna mat bhoolna

approach.hi: Nearest Neighbor Heuristic: City 0 se shuru karo. Har step pe sabse closest unvisited city pe jao. Saari cities visit karne ke baad start pe wapas aao. Ye ek greedy O(n^2) approximation hai.

code.python:
def tsp_nearest_neighbor(dist, n):
    visited = [False] * n
    path = [0]
    visited[0] = True
    total = 0
    curr = 0
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        nearest = min(
            (j for j in range(n) if not visited[j]),
            key=lambda j: dist[curr][j]
        )
        total += dist[curr][nearest]
        visited[nearest] = True
        path.append(nearest)
        curr = nearest
    total += dist[curr][0]
    path.append(0)
    return total, path

problems.title: Satisfiability Check

description.en:
Given a Boolean formula in Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) with n variables and m clauses, determine if there exists an assignment of truth values to the variables that makes the entire formula TRUE. Print 'SATISFIABLE' followed by the assignment, or 'UNSATISFIABLE'.

Each clause is a disjunction (OR) of literals. A literal is either a variable (x_i) or its negation (-x_i). The formula is a conjunction (AND) of all clauses.

Input format: First line has n (variables) and m (clauses). Next m lines each have a clause: space-separated integers where positive i means x_i is true and negative -i means x_i is false, ending with 0.
description.hi:
Ek Boolean formula diya hai Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) mein jisme n variables aur m clauses hain. Batao ki kya variables ko koi aisi truth values assign ki ja sakti hain ki poora formula TRUE ho jaye. 'SATISFIABLE' print karo assignment ke saath, ya 'UNSATISFIABLE' print karo.

Har clause ek disjunction (OR) hai literals ka. Literal ek variable (x_i) ya uska negation (-x_i) hota hai. Formula saare clauses ka conjunction (AND) hai.

Input format: Pehli line mein n (variables) aur m (clauses). Agle m lines mein har ek clause hai: space-separated integers jahan positive i ka matlab x_i true hai aur negative -i ka matlab x_i false hai, 0 se end hota hai.

explanation.en: x1=T, x2=F, x3=F satisfies all clauses: (T OR T)=T, (F OR F)=F... Let's check: clause1: x1 OR NOT x2 = T OR T = T, clause2: x2 OR x3 = F OR F = F. Actually x1=T, x2=T, x3=F: clause1: T OR F = T, clause2: T OR F = T, clause3: F OR T = T. Assignment: 1 2 -3
explanation.hi: x1=T, x2=T, x3=F se saare clauses satisfy hote hain: clause1: x1 OR NOT x2 = T OR F = T, clause2: x2 OR x3 = T OR F = T, clause3: NOT x1 OR NOT x3 = F OR T = T

explanation.en: x1 must be both TRUE and FALSE - impossible
explanation.hi: x1 ko TRUE bhi hona chahiye aur FALSE bhi - impossible

constraints: Each clause has at least 1 literal

hints.en: Try all 2^n assignments using brute force (bitmask) since n is small
hints.hi: Saare 2^n assignments try karo brute force (bitmask) se kyunki n chhota hai

hints.en: For each assignment, check if all clauses are satisfied
hints.hi: Har assignment ke liye check karo ki saare clauses satisfy hote hain ya nahi

starterCode.python:
def solve_sat(n, clauses):
    # Determine if the CNF formula is satisfiable
    # Return (True, assignment) or (False, None)
    # Write your code here
    pass

n, m = map(int, input().split())
clauses = []
for _ in range(m):
    clause = list(map(int, input().split()))
    clause.pop()  # remove trailing 0
    clauses.append(clause)
result = solve_sat(n, clauses)
if result[0]:
    print("SATISFIABLE")
    print(*result[1])
else:
    print("UNSATISFIABLE")

approach.en: Brute force: try all 2^n truth assignments using bitmask. For each assignment, evaluate all clauses. A clause is satisfied if at least one literal is true. The formula is satisfied if all clauses are satisfied.
approach.hi: Brute force: bitmask se saare 2^n truth assignments try karo. Har assignment ke liye saare clauses evaluate karo. Ek clause satisfy hota hai agar kam se kam ek literal true ho. Formula satisfy hota hai agar saare clauses satisfy hon.

solution.timeComplexity: O(2^n * m * L) where L is max clause length
